  - `left` - The element's CSS `left` value. Units must be supplied.

  - `top` - The element's CSS `top` value. Units must be supplied.

  - `width` - The element's CSS `width` value. Units must be supplied.

  - `height` - The element's CSS `height` value. Units must be supplied.

  - `scrollLeft` - The element's `scrollLeft` value.

  - `scrollTop` - The element's `scrollTop` value.

  - `opacity` - The element's `opacity` value. This must be a value between `0` and `1`.

**Be aware** that animating an Element which is being used by an Ext Component without in some way informing the
Component about the changed element state will result in incorrect Component behaviour. This is because the
Component will be using the old state of the element. To avoid this problem, it is now possible to directly
animate certain properties of Components.

items.name: Ext.dom.Query
items.text:
Provides high performance selector/xpath processing by compiling queries into reusable functions. New pseudo classes
and matchers can be plugged. It works on HTML and XML documents (if a content node is passed in).

DomQuery supports most of the [CSS3 selectors spec][1], along with some custom selectors and basic XPath.

All selectors, attribute filters and pseudos below can be combined infinitely in any order. For example
`div.foo:nth-child(odd)[@foo=bar].bar:first` would be a perfectly valid selector. Node filters are processed
in the order in which they appear, which allows you to optimize your queries for your document structure.

## Element Selectors:

  - **`*`** any element
  - **`E`** an element with the tag E
  - **`E F`** All descendent elements of E that have the tag F
  - **`E > F`** or **E/F** all direct children elements of E that have the tag F
  - **`E + F`** all elements with the tag F that are immediately preceded by an element with the tag E
  - **`E ~ F`** all elements with the tag F that are preceded by a sibling element with the tag E

## Attribute Selectors:

The use of `@` and quotes are optional. For example, `div[@foo='bar']` is also a valid attribute selector.

  - **`E[foo]`** has an attribute "foo"
  - **`E[foo=bar]`** has an attribute "foo" that equals "bar"
  - **`E[foo^=bar]`** has an attribute "foo" that starts with "bar"
  - **`E[foo$=bar]`** has an attribute "foo" that ends with "bar"
  - **`E[foo*=bar]`** has an attribute "foo" that contains the substring "bar"
  - **`E[foo%=2]`** has an attribute "foo" that is evenly divisible by 2
  - **`E[foo!=bar]`** attribute "foo" does not equal "bar"

## Pseudo Classes:

  - **`E:first-child`** E is the first child of its parent
  - **`E:last-child`** E is the last child of its parent
  - **`E:nth-child(_n_)`** E is the _n_th child of its parent (1 based as per the spec)
  - **`E:nth-child(odd)`** E is an odd child of its parent
  - **`E:nth-child(even)`** E is an even child of its parent
  - **`E:only-child`** E is the only child of its parent
  - **`E:checked`** E is an element that is has a checked attribute that is true (e.g. a radio or checkbox)
  - **`E:first`** the first E in the resultset
  - **`E:last`** the last E in the resultset
  - **`E:nth(_n_)`** the _n_th E in the resultset (1 based)
  - **`E:odd`** shortcut for :nth-child(odd)
  - **`E:even`** shortcut for :nth-child(even)
  - **`E:contains(foo)`** E's innerHTML contains the substring "foo"
  - **`E:nodeValue(foo)`** E contains a textNode with a nodeValue that equals "foo"
  - **`E:not(S)`** an E element that does not match simple selector S
  - **`E:has(S)`** an E element that has a descendent that matches simple selector S
  - **`E:next(S)`** an E element whose next sibling matches simple selector S
  - **`E:prev(S)`** an E element whose previous sibling matches simple selector S
  - **`E:any(S1|S2|S2)`** an E element which matches any of the simple selectors S1, S2 or S3

## CSS Value Selectors:

  - **`E{display=none}`** css value "display" that equals "none"
  - **`E{display^=none}`** css value "display" that starts with "none"
  - **`E{display$=none}`** css value "display" that ends with "none"
  - **`E{display*=none}`** css value "display" that contains the substring "none"
  - **`E{display%=2}`** css value "display" that is evenly divisible by 2
  - **`E{display!=none}`** css value "display" that does not equal "none"

## XML Namespaces:
  - **`ns|E`** an element with tag E and namespace prefix ns

[1]: http://www.w3.org/TR/2005/WD-css3-selectors-20051215/#selectors

Exports a {@link Ext.draw.Surface} to an image. To do this,
the svg string must be sent to a remote server and processed.

# Sending the data

A post request is made to the URL. The following fields are sent:

+ width: The width of the image
+ height: The height of the image
+ type: The image type to save as, see {@link #property!supportedTypes #supportedTypes}
+ svg: The svg string for the surface

# The response

It is expected that the user will be prompted with an image download.
As such, the following options should be set on the server:

+ Content-Disposition: 'attachment, filename="chart.png"'
+ Content-Type: 'image/png'

**Important**: By default, chart data is sent to a server operated
by Sencha to do data processing. You may change this default by
setting the {@link #property!defaultUrl #defaultUrl} of this class.

items.name: Ext.draw.Surface
items.text:
A Surface is an interface to render methods inside {@link Ext.draw.Component}.

Most of the Surface methods are abstract and they have a concrete implementation
in {@link Ext.draw.engine.Vml} or {@link Ext.draw.engine.Svg} engines.

A Surface contains methods to render {@link Ext.draw.Sprite}, get bounding
boxes of sprites, add sprites to the canvas, initialize other graphic components, etc.

## Adding sprites to surface

One of the most used methods for this class is the {@link #method!add #add} method, to add Sprites to
the surface. For example:

    drawComponent.surface.add({
        type: 'circle',
        fill: '#ffc',
        radius: 100,
        x: 100,
        y: 100
    });

The configuration object passed in the `{@link #method!add add}` method is the same as described in the
{@link Ext.draw.Sprite} class documentation.

Sprites can also be added to surface by setting their surface config at creation time:

    var sprite = Ext.create('Ext.draw.Sprite', {
        type: 'circle',
        fill: '#ff0',
        surface: drawComponent.surface,
        radius: 5
    });

In order to properly apply properties and render the sprite we have to
`show` the sprite setting the option `redraw` to `true`:

    sprite.show(true);

items.name: Ext.EventManager
items.text:
Registers event handlers that want to receive a normalized EventObject instead of the standard browser event and provides
several useful events directly.

See {@link Ext.EventObject} for more details on normalized event objects.

items.name: addListener
items.text:
Appends an event handler to an element.  The shorthand version {@link #method!on #on} is equivalent.
Typically you will use {@link Ext.dom.Element#method!addListener Ext.Element#addListener} directly on an Element in favor of
calling this version.

{@link Ext.EventManager#method!on Ext.EventManager#on} is an alias for {@link Ext.EventManager#method!addListener Ext.EventManager#addListener}.

items.name: el
items.text: The html element or id to assign the event handler to.

items.name: eventName
items.text: The name of the event to listen for.

items.name: handler
items.text: The handler function the event invokes.

items.name: event
items.text: The {@link Ext.EventObject} describing the event.

items.name: target
items.text:
The Element which was the target of the event.
Note that this may be filtered by using the `delegate` option.

items.name: options
items.text: The options object from the addListener call.

items.name: scope
items.text:
The scope (`this` reference) in which the handler function is executed.
Defaults to the Element.

Causes the handler to be scheduled to run in an {@link Ext.util.DelayedTask} delayed
by the specified number of milliseconds. If the event fires again within that time, the original
handler is *not* invoked, but the new handler is scheduled in its place.

*not* if the event was bubbled up from a child node.

items.name: pollScroll
items.text:
This strategy has minimal benefits for Sencha solutions that build themselves (ie. minimal initial page markup).
However, progressively-enhanced pages (with image content and/or embedded frames) will benefit the most from it.
Browser timer resolution is too poor to ensure a doScroll check more than once on a page loaded with minimal
assets (the readystatechange event 'complete' usually beats the doScroll timer on a 'lightly-loaded' initial document).

items.name: Ext.FocusManager
items.text:
The FocusManager is responsible for globally:

1. Managing component focus
2. Providing basic keyboard navigation
3. (optional) Provide a visual cue for focused components, in the form of a focus ring/frame.

To activate the FocusManager, simply call `Ext.FocusManager.enable();`. In turn, you may
deactivate the FocusManager by subsequently calling `Ext.FocusManager.disable();`.  The
FocusManager is disabled by default.

To enable the optional focus frame, pass `true` or `{focusFrame: true}` to {@link #method!enable #method-enable}.

Another feature of the FocusManager is to provide basic keyboard focus navigation scoped to any {@link Ext.container.Container}
that would like to have navigation between its child {@link Ext.Component}'s.

items.name: whitelist
items.text:
A list of xtypes that should ignore certain navigation input keys and
allow for the default browser event/behavior. These input keys include:

1. Backspace
2. Delete
3. Left
4. Right
5. Up
6. Down

The FocusManager will not attempt to navigate when a component is an xtype (or descendents thereof)
that belongs to this whitelist. E.g., an {@link Ext.form.field.Text} should allow
the user to move the input cursor left and right, and to delete characters, etc.

items.name: Ext.form.action.Action
items.text:
The subclasses of this class provide actions to perform upon {@link Ext.form.Basic}s.

Instances of this class are only created by a {@link Ext.form.Basic} when the Form needs to perform an action
such as submit or load. The Configuration options listed for this class are set through the Form's action methods:
{@link Ext.form.Basic#method!submit submit}, {@link Ext.form.Basic#method!load load} and {@link Ext.form.Basic#method!doAction doAction}

The instance of Action which performed the action is passed to the success and failure callbacks of the Form's action
methods ({@link Ext.form.Basic#method!submit submit}, {@link Ext.form.Basic#method!load load} and
{@link Ext.form.Basic#method!doAction doAction}), and to the {@link Ext.form.Basic#event!actioncomplete actioncomplete} and
{@link Ext.form.Basic#event!actionfailed actionfailed} event handlers.

items.name: failure
items.text: The function to call when a failure packet was received, or when an error ocurred in the Ajax communication.

items.name: form
items.text: The form that requested the action

items.name: action
items.text:
The Action class. If an Ajax error ocurred, the failure type will
be in {@link #property!failureType #failureType}. The {@link #property!result #result} property of this object may be examined to perform custom
postprocessing.

items.name: form
items.text: The {@link Ext.form.Basic} instance that is invoking this Action. Required.

items.name: headers
items.text:
Extra headers to be sent in the AJAX request for submit and load actions.
See {@link Ext.data.proxy.Ajax#cfg!headers Ext.data.proxy.Ajax#headers}.

items.name: method
items.text:
The HTTP method to use to access the requested URL.
Defaults to the {@link Ext.form.Basic#cfg!method BasicForm's method}, or 'POST' if not specified.

items.name: params
items.text:
Extra parameter values to pass. These are added to the Form's {@link Ext.form.Basic#cfg!baseParams Ext.form.Basic#baseParams} and passed to the
specified URL along with the Form's input fields.

Parameters are encoded as standard HTTP parameters using {@link Ext#method!urlEncode Ext.Object.toQueryString}.

items.name: reset
items.text:
When set to **true**, causes the Form to be {@link Ext.form.Basic#method!reset reset} on Action success. If specified,
this happens before the {@link #cfg!success #success} callback is called and before the Form's
{@link Ext.form.Basic#event!actioncomplete actioncomplete} event fires.

items.name: scope
items.text:
The scope in which to call the configured #success and #failure callback functions
(the `this` reference for the callback functions).

items.name: submitEmptyText
items.text: If set to true, the emptyText value will be sent with the form when it is submitted.

items.name: success
items.text: The function to call when a valid success return packet is received.

items.name: form
items.text: The form that requested the action

items.name: action
items.text:
The Action class. The {@link #property!result #result} property of this object may
be examined to perform custom postprocessing.

items.name: timeout
items.text:
The number of seconds to wait for a server response before failing with the {@link #property!failureType #failureType} as
{@link Ext.form.action.Action#static-property!CONNECT_FAILURE Ext.form.action.Action#CONNECT_FAILURE}. If not specified, defaults to the configured
{@link Ext.form.Basic#cfg!timeout timeout} of the {@link #cfg!form #form}.

items.name: url
items.text:
The URL that the Action is to invoke. Will default to the {@link Ext.form.Basic#cfg!url url} configured on the
{@link #cfg!form #form}.

items.name: waitMsg
items.text:
The message to be displayed by a call to {@link Ext.window.MessageBox#method!wait Ext.window.MessageBox#wait} during the time the action is being
processed.

items.name: waitTitle
items.text:
The title to be displayed by a call to {@link Ext.window.MessageBox#method!wait Ext.window.MessageBox#wait} during the time the action is being
processed.

items.name: CLIENT_INVALID
items.text:
Failure type returned when client side validation of the Form fails thus aborting a submit action. Client
side validation is performed unless {@link Ext.form.action.Submit#cfg!clientValidation Ext.form.action.Submit#clientValidation} is explicitly set to
false.

items.name: CONNECT_FAILURE
items.text:
Failure type returned when a communication error happens when attempting to send a request to the remote
server. The {@link #property!response #response} may be examined to provide further information.

items.name: LOAD_FAILURE
items.text:
Failure type returned when the response's `{@link #cfg!success success}` property is set to false, or no field values are returned
in the response's data property.

items.name: SERVER_INVALID
items.text:
Failure type returned when server side processing fails and the {@link #property!result #result}'s `{@link #cfg!success success}` property is set to
false.

In the case of a form submission, field-specific error messages may be returned in the {@link #property!result #result}'s
errors property.

Ext.form.action.StandardSubmit
items.text:
A class which handles submission of data from {@link Ext.form.Basic}s using a standard `<form>` element submit.
It does not handle the response from the submit.

If validation of the form fields fails, the Form's afterAction method will be called. Otherwise, afterAction will not
be called.

Instances of this class are only created by a {@link Ext.form.Basic} when
{@link Ext.form.Basic#method!submit submit}ting, when the form's {@link Ext.form.Basic#cfg!standardSubmit Ext.form.Basic#standardSubmit} config option is true.

items.name: target
items.text:
Optional target attribute to be used for the form when submitting.

Defaults to the current window/frame.

items.name: doSubmit
items.text:
Perform the form submit. Creates and submits a temporary form element containing an input element for each
field value returned by {@link Ext.form.Basic#method!getValues Ext.form.Basic#getValues}, plus any configured {@link #cfg!params params} or
{@link Ext.form.Basic#cfg!baseParams baseParams}.

items.name: Ext.form.action.Submit
items.text: A class which handles submission of data from {@link Ext.form.Basic}s and processes the returned response. Instances of this class are only created by a {@link Ext.form.Basic} when {@link Ext.form.Basic#method!submit submit}ting. # Response Packet Criteria A response packet may contain: - **`{@link #cfg!success success}`** property : Boolean - required. - **`errors`** property : Object - optional, contains error messages for invalid fields. # JSON Packets By default, response packets are assumed to be JSON, so a typical response packet may look like this: { success: false, errors: { clientCode: "Client not found", portOfLoading: "This field must not be null" } } Other data may be placed into the response for processing by the {@link Ext.form.Basic}'s callback or event handler methods. The object decoded from this JSON is available in the {@link Ext.form.action.Action#property!result result} property. Alternatively, if an {@link Ext.form.Basic#cfg!errorReader errorReader} is specified as an {@link Ext.data.reader.Xml}: errorReader: new Ext.data.reader.Xml({ record : 'field', success: '@success' }, [ 'id', 'msg' ] ) then the results may be sent back in XML format: clientCode This is a test validation message from the server ]]> portOfLoading This is a test validation message from the server ]]> Other elements may be placed into the response XML for processing by the {@link Ext.form.Basic}'s callback or event handler methods. The XML document is available in the {@link Ext.form.Basic#cfg!errorReader errorReader}'s {@link Ext.data.reader.Xml#property!xmlData xmlData} property.

items.name: clientValidation
items.text:
Determines whether a Form's fields are validated in a final call to {@link Ext.form.Basic#method!isValid isValid} prior
to submission. Pass false in the Form's submit options to prevent this.

items.name: buildForm
items.text:
Builds a form element containing fields corresponding to all the parameters to be
submitted (everything returned by {@link #method!getParams #getParams}.

NOTE: the form element is automatically added to the DOM, so any code that uses
it must remove it from the DOM after finishing with it.

items.name: doSubmit
items.text: Performs the submit of the form data.

items.name: getParams
items.text: Builds the full set of parameters from the field values plus any additional configured params.

items.name: Ext.form.Basic
api
items.text:
If specified, load and submit actions will be handled with {@link Ext.form.action.DirectLoad}
and {@link Ext.form.action.DirectSubmit}.  Methods which have been imported by
{@link Ext.direct.Manager} can be specified here to load and submit forms. API methods may also be
specified as strings. See {@link Ext.data.proxy.Direct#cfg!directFn Ext.data.proxy.Direct#directFn}.  Such as the following:

    api: {
        load: App.ss.MyProfile.load,
        submit: App.ss.MyProfile.submit
    }

Load actions can use {@link #cfg!paramOrder #paramOrder} or {@link #cfg!paramsAsHash #paramsAsHash} to customize how the load method
is invoked.  Submit actions will always use a standard form submit. The `formHandler` configuration
(see Ext.direct.RemotingProvider#action) must be set on the associated server-side method which has
been imported by {@link Ext.direct.Manager}.

items.name: baseParams
items.text:
Parameters to pass with all requests. e.g. baseParams: `{id: '123', foo: 'bar'}`.

Parameters are encoded as standard HTTP parameters using {@link Ext.Object#method!toQueryString Ext.Object#toQueryString}.

items.name: errorReader
items.text:
An Ext.data.reader.Reader (e.g. {@link Ext.data.reader.Xml}) instance or
configuration to be used to read field error messages returned from 'submit' actions.
This is optional as there is built-in support for processing JSON responses.

The Records which provide messages for the invalid Fields must use the
Field name (or id) as the Record ID, and must contain a field called 'msg'
which contains the error message.

The errorReader does not have to be a full-blown implementation of a
Reader. It simply needs to implement a `read(xhr)` function
which returns an Array of Records in an object with the following
structure:

    {
        records: recordArray
    }

items.name: jsonSubmit
method
items.text: The request method to use (GET or POST) for form actions if one isn't supplied in the action options.

items.name: paramOrder
items.text:
A list of params to be executed server side. Only used for the {@link #cfg!api #api} `{@link #method!load load}`
configuration.

Specify the params in the order in which they must be executed on the
server-side as either (1) an Array of String values, or (2) a String of params
delimited by either whitespace, comma, or pipe. For example,
any of the following would be acceptable:

    paramOrder: ['param1','param2','param3']
    paramOrder: 'param1 param2 param3'
    paramOrder: 'param1,param2,param3'
    paramOrder: 'param1|param2|param'

items.name: paramsAsHash
items.text:
Only used for the {@link #cfg!api #api} `{@link #method!load load}` configuration. If true, parameters will be sent as a
single hash collection of named arguments. Providing a {@link #cfg!paramOrder #paramOrder} nullifies this
configuration.

items.name: reader
items.text:
An Ext.data.reader.Reader (e.g. {@link Ext.data.reader.Xml}) instance or
configuration to be used to read data when executing 'load' actions. This
is optional as there is built-in support for processing JSON responses.

items.name: hasUpload
items.text:
Returns `true` if the form contains a file upload field. This is used to determine the method for submitting the
form: File uploads are not performed using normal 'Ajax' techniques, that is they are **not** performed using
XMLHttpRequests. Instead a hidden `<form>` element containing all the fields is created temporarily and submitted
with its [target][1] set to refer to a dynamically generated, hidden `<iframe>` which is inserted into the document
but removed after the return data has been gathered.

The server response is parsed by the browser to create the document for the IFRAME. If the server is using JSON
to send the return object, then the [Content-Type][2] header must be set to "text/html" in order to tell the
browser to insert the text unchanged into the document body.

Characters which are significant to an HTML parser must be sent as HTML entities, so encode `"<"` as `"<"`,
`"&"` as `"&"` etc.

The response text is retrieved from the document, and a fake XMLHttpRequest object is created containing a
responseText property in order to conform to the requirements of event handlers and callbacks.

Be aware that file upload packets are sent with the content type [multipart/form][3] and some server technologies
(notably JEE) may require some custom processing in order to retrieve parameter names and parameter values from
the packet content.

[1]: http://www.w3.org/TR/REC-html40/present/frames.html#adef-target
[2]: http://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec14.html#sec14.17
[3]: http://www.faqs.org/rfcs/rfc2388.html

items.name: Ext.form.CheckboxGroup
items.text:
A {@link Ext.form.FieldContainer} which has a specialized layout for arranging
{@link Ext.form.field.Checkbox} controls into columns, and provides convenience
{@link Ext.form.field.Field} methods for {@link #method!getValue getting}, {@link #method!setValue setting},
and {@link #method!validate validating} the group of checkboxes as a whole.

# Validation

Individual checkbox fields themselves have no default validation behavior, but
sometimes you want to require a user to select at least one of a group of checkboxes. CheckboxGroup
allows this by setting the config `{@link #cfg!allowBlank #allowBlank}:false`; when the user does not check at
least one of the checkboxes, the entire group will be highlighted as invalid and the
{@link #cfg!blankText error message} will be displayed according to the {@link #cfg!msgTarget #msgTarget} config.

# Layout

The default layout for CheckboxGroup makes it easy to arrange the checkboxes into
columns; see the {@link #cfg!columns #columns} and {@link #cfg!vertical #vertical} config documentation for details. You may also
use a completely different layout by setting the {@link #cfg!layout #layout} to one of the other supported layout
types; for instance you may wish to use a custom arrangement of hbox and vbox containers. In that case
the checkbox components at any depth will still be managed by the CheckboxGroup's validation.

    @example
    Ext.create('Ext.form.Panel', {
        title: 'Checkbox Group',
        width: 300,
        height: 125,
        bodyPadding: 10,
        renderTo: Ext.getBody(),
        items:[{
            xtype: 'checkboxgroup',
            fieldLabel: 'Two Columns',
            // Arrange checkboxes into two columns, distributed vertically
            columns: 2,
            vertical: true,
            items: [
                { boxLabel: 'Item 1', name: 'rb', inputValue: '1' },
                { boxLabel: 'Item 2', name: 'rb', inputValue: '2', checked: true },
                { boxLabel: 'Item 3', name: 'rb', inputValue: '3' },
                { boxLabel: 'Item 4', name: 'rb', inputValue: '4' },
                { boxLabel: 'Item 5', name: 'rb', inputValue: '5' },
                { boxLabel: 'Item 6', name: 'rb', inputValue: '6' }
            ]
        }]
    });

items.name: allowBlank
items.text:
False to validate that at least one item in the group is checked. If no items are selected at
validation time, {@link #cfg!blankText #blankText} will be used as the error text.

items.name: blankText
items.text: Error text to display if the {@link #cfg!allowBlank #allowBlank} validation fails
items.value: "You must select at least one item in this group"

items.name: columns
items.text:
Specifies the number of columns to use when displaying grouped checkbox/radio controls using automatic layout.
This config can take several types of values:

- 'auto' - The controls will be rendered one per column on one row and the width of each column will be evenly
  distributed based on the width of the overall field container. This is the default.
- Number - If you specific a number (e.g., 3) that number of columns will be created and the contained controls
  will be automatically distributed based on the value of {@link #cfg!vertical #vertical}.
- Array - You can also specify an array of column widths, mixing integer (fixed width) and float (percentage
  width) values as needed (e.g., [100, .25, .75]). Any integer values will be rendered first, then any float
  values will be calculated as a percentage of the remaining space. Float values do not have to add up to 1
  (100%) although if you want the controls to take up the entire field container you should do so.

items.name: fieldBodyCls
items.text: An extra CSS class to be applied to the body content element in addition to {@link #cfg!baseBodyCls #baseBodyCls}.

items.name: items
items.text: An Array of {@link Ext.form.field.Checkbox}es or Checkbox config objects to arrange in the group.

items.name: vertical
items.text:
True to distribute contained controls across columns, completely filling each column top to bottom before
starting on the next column. The number of controls in each column will be automatically calculated to keep
columns as even as possible. The default value is false, so that controls will be added to columns one at a time,
completely filling each row left to right before starting on the next row.

Array of Ext.form.field.Checkbox components

Runs CheckboxGroup's validations and returns an array of any errors. The only error by default is if allowBlank
is set to true and no items are checked.
Array of all validation errors

items.name: getValue
items.text:
Returns an object containing the values of all checked checkboxes within the group. Each key-value pair in the
object corresponds to a checkbox {@link Ext.form.field.Checkbox#cfg!name name}. If there is only one checked checkbox
with a particular name, the value of that pair will be the String {@link Ext.form.field.Checkbox#cfg!inputValue inputValue} of that checkbox. If there are multiple checked checkboxes with that name, the value of that pair
will be an Array of the selected inputValues.

The object format returned from this method can also be passed directly to the {@link #method!setValue #setValue} method.

NOTE: In Ext 3, this method returned an array of Checkbox components; this was changed to make it more consistent
with other field components and with the {@link #method!setValue #setValue} argument signature. If you need the old behavior in
Ext 4+, use the {@link #method!getChecked #getChecked} method instead.

after they have been initialized.

checkChangeBuffer
items.text:
Defines a timeout in milliseconds for buffering {@link #cfg!checkChangeEvents #checkChangeEvents} that fire in rapid succession.
Defaults to 50 milliseconds.

items.name: checkChangeEvents
items.text:
A list of event names that will be listened for on the field's {@link #property!inputEl input element}, which will cause
the field's value to be checked for changes. If a change is detected, the {@link #event!change change event} will be
fired, followed by validation if the {@link #cfg!validateOnChange #validateOnChange} option is enabled.

Defaults to ['change', 'propertychange', 'keyup'] in Internet Explorer, and ['change', 'input', 'textInput', 'keyup',
'dragdrop'] in other browsers. This catches all the ways that field values can be changed in most supported
browsers; the only known exceptions at the time of writing are:

  - Safari 3.2 and older: cut/paste in textareas via the context menu, and dragging text into textareas
  - Opera 10 and 11: dragging text into text fields and textareas, and cut via the context menu in text fields
    and textareas
  - Opera 9: Same as Opera 10 and 11, plus paste from context menu in text fields and textareas

If you need to guarantee on-the-fly change notifications including these edge cases, you can call the
{@link #method!checkChange #checkChange} method on a repeating interval, e.g. using {@link Ext.util.TaskManager Ext.TaskManager}, or if the field is within
a {@link Ext.form.Panel}, you can use the FormPanel's {@link Ext.form.Panel#cfg!pollForChanges Ext.form.Panel#pollForChanges} configuration to set up
such a task automatically.

    '<input id="{id}" type="{type}" {inputAttrTpl}',
    ' size="1"',
    // allows inputs to fully respect CSS widths across all browsers
    '<tpl if="name"> name="{name}"</tpl>',
    '<tpl if="value"> value="{[Ext.util.Format.htmlEncode(values.value)]}"</tpl>',
    '<tpl if="placeholder"> placeholder="{placeholder}"</tpl>',
    '{%if (values.maxLength !== undefined){%} maxlength="{maxLength}"{%}%}',
    '<tpl if="readOnly"> readonly="readonly"</tpl>',
    '<tpl if="disabled"> disabled="disabled"</tpl>',
    '<tpl if="tabIdx"> tabIndex="{tabIdx}"</tpl>',
    '<tpl if="fieldStyle"> style="{fieldStyle}"</tpl>',
    ' class="{fieldCls} {typeCls} {editableCls}" autocomplete="off"/>',
    {
        disableFormats: true

]

items.name: inputAttrTpl
items.text:
An optional string or `XTemplate` configuration to insert in the field markup
inside the input element (as attributes). If an `XTemplate` is used, the component's
{@link #method!getSubTplData subTpl data} serves as the context.

items.name: inputId
items.text:
The id that will be given to the generated input DOM element. Defaults to an automatically generated id. If you
configure this manually, you must make sure it is unique in the document.

items.name: inputType
items.text:
The type attribute for input fields -- e.g. radio, text, password, file. The extended types
supported by HTML5 inputs (url, email, etc.) may also be used, though using them will cause older browsers to
fall back to 'text'.

The type 'password' must be used to render that field type currently -- there is no separate Ext component for
that. You can use {@link Ext.form.field.File} which creates a custom-rendered file upload field, but if you want
a plain unstyled file input you can use a Base with inputType:'file'.

items.name: invalidText
items.text: The error text to use when marking a field invalid and no message is provided
items.value: 'The value in this field is invalid'

items.name: name
items.text:
The name of the field. This is used as the parameter name when including the field value
in a {@link Ext.form.Basic#method!submit form submit()}. If no name is configured, it falls back to the {@link #cfg!inputId #inputId}.
To prevent the field from being included in the form submit, set {@link #cfg!submitValue #submitValue} to false.

items.name: readOnly
items.text:
true to mark the field as readOnly in HTML.

**Note**: this only sets the element's readOnly DOM attribute. Setting `readOnly=true`, for example, will not
disable triggering a ComboBox or Date; it gives you the option of forcing the user to choose via the trigger
without typing in the text box. To hide the trigger use `{@link Ext.form.field.Trigger#cfg!hideTrigger hideTrigger}`.

applyTo

items.name: validateOnBlur
items.text:

as the user steps through the fields in the form regardless of whether they are making changes to those fields
along the way. See also {@link #cfg!validateOnChange #validateOnChange}.

items.text:
Clear any invalid styles/messages for this field.

**Note**: this method does not cause the Field's {@link #method!validate #validate} or {@link #method!isValid #isValid} methods to return `true`
if the value does not _pass_ validation. So simply clearing a field's errors will not necessarily allow
submission of forms submitted with the {@link Ext.form.action.Submit#cfg!clientValidation Ext.form.action.Submit#clientValidation} option set.

normalized and converted value see {@link #method!getValue #getValue}.

items.name: getSubmitValue
items.text:
Returns the value that would be included in a standard form submit for this field. This will be combined with the
field's name to form a name=value pair in the {@link #method!getSubmitData submitted parameters}. If an empty string is
returned then just the name= will be submitted; if null is returned then nothing will be submitted.

Note that the value returned will have been {@link #method!processRawValue processed} but may or may not have been
successfully {@link #method!validate validated}.
The value to be submitted, or null.

items.name: getSubTplData
items.text: Creates and returns the data object to be used when rendering the {@link #cfg!fieldSubTpl #fieldSubTpl}.
The template data

items.name: getSubTplMarkup
items.text: Gets the markup to be inserted into the outer template's bodyEl. For fields this is the actual input element.

items.name: getValue
items.text:
Returns the current data value of the field. The type of value returned is particular to the type of the
particular field (e.g. a Date object for {@link Ext.form.field.Date}), as the result of calling {@link #method!rawToValue #rawToValue} on
the field's {@link #method!processRawValue processed} String value. To return the raw String value, see {@link #method!getRawValue #getRawValue}.
value The field value

items.name: isValid
items.text:
Returns whether or not the field value is currently valid by {@link #method!getErrors validating} the
{@link #method!processRawValue processed raw value} of the field. **Note**: {@link #cfg!disabled #disabled} fields are
always treated as valid.
True if the value is valid, else false

items.name: markInvalid
items.text:
Display one or more error messages associated with this field, using {@link #cfg!msgTarget #msgTarget} to determine how to
display the messages and applying {@link #cfg!invalidCls #invalidCls} to the field's UI element.

**Note**: this method does not cause the Field's {@link #method!validate #validate} or {@link #method!isValid #isValid} methods to return `false`
if the value does _pass_ validation. So simply marking a Field as invalid will not prevent submission of forms
submitted with the {@link Ext.form.action.Submit#cfg!clientValidation Ext.form.action.Submit#clientValidation} option set.

items.name: errors
items.text: The validation message(s) to display.

items.name: processRawValue
items.text:
Performs any necessary manipulation of a raw field value to prepare it for {@link #method!rawToValue conversion} and/or
{@link #method!validate validation}, for instance stripping out ignored characters. In the base implementation it does
nothing; individual subclasses may override this as needed.

items.name: value
items.text: The unprocessed string value
The processed string value

items.name: rawToValue
items.text:
Converts a raw input field value into a mixed-type value that is suitable for this particular field type. This
allows controlling the normalization and conversion of user-entered values into field-type-appropriate values,
e.g. a Date object for {@link Ext.form.field.Date}, and is invoked by {@link #method!getValue #getValue}.

It is up to individual implementations to decide how to handle raw values that cannot be successfully converted
to the desired object type.

See {@link #method!valueToRaw #valueToRaw} for the opposite conversion.

The base implementation does no conversion, returning the raw value untouched.
The converted value.

Ext.Element#applyStyles}.

items.text:
Sets the field's raw value directly, bypassing {@link #method!valueToRaw value conversion}, change detection, and
validation. To set the value with these additional inspections see {@link #method!setValue #setValue}.

Sets a data value into the field and runs the change detection and validation. To set the value directly
without these inspections see {@link #method!setRawValue #setRawValue}.

this

items.name: validateValue
items.text:
Uses {@link #method!getErrors #getErrors} to build an array of validation errors. If any errors are found, they are passed to
{@link #method!markInvalid #markInvalid} and false is returned, otherwise true is returned.

Previously, subclasses were invited to provide an implementation of this to process validations - from 3.2
onwards {@link #method!getErrors #getErrors} should be overridden instead.

items.text: The value to validate
True if all validations passed, false if one or more failed

items.name: valueToRaw
items.text:

items.name: queryMode
items.text:
The mode in which the ComboBox uses the configured Store. Acceptable values are:

  - **`'remote'`** :

    In `queryMode: 'remote'`, the ComboBox loads its Store dynamically based upon user interaction.

    This is typically used for "autocomplete" type inputs, and after the user finishes typing, the Store is {@link Ext.data.Store#method!load load}ed.

    A parameter containing the typed string is sent in the load request. The default parameter name for the input
    string is `query`, but this can be configured using the {@link #cfg!queryParam #queryParam} config.

    In `queryMode: 'remote'`, the Store may be configured with `{@link Ext.data.Store#cfg!remoteFilter remoteFilter}:
    true`, and further filters may be _programatically_ added to the Store which are then passed with every load
    request which allows the server to further refine the returned dataset.

    Typically, in an autocomplete situation, {@link #cfg!hideTrigger #hideTrigger} is configured `true` because it has no meaning for
    autocomplete.

  - **`'local'`** :

    ComboBox loads local data

        var combo = new Ext.form.field.ComboBox({
            renderTo: document.body,
            queryMode: 'local',
            store: new Ext.data.ArrayStore({
                id: 0,
                fields: [
                    'myId',  // numeric value is the key
                    'displayText'
                ],
                data: [[1, 'item1'], [2, 'item2']]  // data is local
            }),
            valueField: 'myId',
            displayField: 'displayText',
            triggerAction: 'all'
        });

  - **an Array** : Arrays will be converted to a {@link Ext.data.Store} internally, automatically generating
    {@link Ext.data.Field#cfg!name field names} to work with all data components.

    - **1-dimensional array** : (e.g., `['Foo','Bar']`)

      A 1-dimensional array will automatically be expanded (each array item will be used for both the combo
      {@link #cfg!valueField #valueField} and {@link #cfg!displayField #displayField})

    - **2-dimensional array** : (e.g., `[['f','Foo'],['b','Bar']]`)

      For a multi-dimensional array, the value in index 0 of each item will be assumed to be the combo
      {@link #cfg!valueField #valueField}, while the value at index 1 is assumed to be the combo {@link #cfg!displayField #displayField}.

See also {@link #cfg!queryMode #queryMode}.

items.name: Ext.form.field.Field
items.text:
This mixin provides a common interface for the logical behavior and state of form fields, including:

- Getter and setter methods for field values
- Events and methods for tracking value and validity changes
- Methods for triggering validation

**NOTE**: When implementing custom fields, it is most likely that you will want to extend the {@link Ext.form.field.Base}
component class rather than using this mixin directly, as BaseField contains additional logic for generating an
actual DOM complete with {@link Ext.form.Labelable} display and a form input field,
plus methods that bind the Field value getters and setters to the input field's value.

If you do want to implement this mixin directly and don't want to extend {@link Ext.form.field.Base}, then
you will most likely want to override the following methods with custom implementations: {@link #method!getValue #getValue},
{@link #method!setValue #setValue}, and {@link #method!getErrors #getErrors}. Other methods may be overridden as needed but their base
implementations should be sufficient for common cases. You will also need to make sure that {@link #method!initField #initField}
is called during the component's initialization.

items.name: disabled
items.text: True to disable the field. Disabled Fields will not be {@link Ext.form.Basic#method!submit submitted}.

items.name: name
items.text:
The name of the field. By default this is used as the parameter name when including the
{@link #method!getSubmitData field value} in a {@link Ext.form.Basic#method!submit form submit()}. To prevent the field from
being included in the form submit, set {@link #cfg!submitValue #submitValue} to false.

items.name: submitValue
items.text:
Setting this to false will prevent the field from being {@link Ext.form.Basic#method!submit submitted} even when it is
not disabled.

items.name: validateOnChange
items.text:
Specifies whether this field should be validated immediately whenever a change in its value is detected.
If the validation results in a change in the field's validity, a {@link #event!validitychange #validitychange} event will be
fired. This allows the field to show feedback about the validity of its contents immediately as the user is
typing.

When set to false, feedback will not be immediate. However the form will still be validated before submitting if
the clientValidation option to {@link Ext.form.Basic#method!doAction Ext.form.Basic#doAction} is enabled, or if the field or form are validated
manually.

See also {@link Ext.form.field.Base#cfg!checkChangeEvents Ext.form.field.Base#checkChangeEvents} for controlling how changes to the field's value are
detected.

items.name: value
items.text: A value to initialize this field with.

items.name: change
items.text: Fires when the value of a field is changed via the {@link #method!setValue #setValue} method.

items.text: The new value

items.name: Ext.form.field.HtmlEditor
items.text:
Provides a lightweight HTML Editor component. Some toolbar features are not supported by Safari and will be
automatically hidden when needed. These are noted in the config options where appropriate.

The editor's toolbar buttons have tooltips defined in the {@link #property!buttonTips #buttonTips} property, but they are not
enabled by default unless the global {@link Ext.tip.QuickTipManager} singleton is
{@link Ext.tip.QuickTipManager#method!init initialized}.

An Editor is a sensitive component that can't be used in all spots standard fields can be used. Putting an
Editor within any element that has display set to 'none' can cause problems in Safari and Firefox due to their
default iframe reloading bugs.

# Example usage

Simple example rendered with default options:

    @example
    Ext.tip.QuickTipManager.init();  // enable tooltips
    Ext.create('Ext.form.HtmlEditor', {
        width: 580,
        height: 250,
        renderTo: Ext.getBody()
    });

Passed via xtype into a container and with custom options:

    @example
    Ext.tip.QuickTipManager.init();  // enable tooltips
    new Ext.panel.Panel({
        title: 'HTML Editor',
        renderTo: Ext.getBody(),
        width: 550,
        height: 250,
        frame: true,
        layout: 'fit',
        items: {
            xtype: 'htmleditor',
            enableColors: false,
            enableAlignments: false
        }
    });

# Reflow issues

In some browsers, a layout reflow will cause the underlying editor iframe to be reset. This
is most commonly seen when using the editor in collapsed panels with animation. In these cases
it is best to avoid animation. More information can be found here: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=90268

items.name: Ext.form.field.Text
items.text:
A basic text field.  Can be used as a direct replacement for traditional text inputs,
or as the base class for more sophisticated input controls (like {@link Ext.form.field.TextArea}
and {@link Ext.form.field.ComboBox}). Has support for empty-field placeholder values (see {@link #cfg!emptyText #emptyText}).

# Validation

The Text field has a useful set of validations built in:

- {@link #cfg!allowBlank #allowBlank} for making the field required
- {@link #cfg!minLength #minLength} for requiring a minimum value length
- {@link #cfg!maxLength #maxLength} for setting a maximum value length (with {@link #cfg!enforceMaxLength #enforceMaxLength} to add it
  as the `maxlength` attribute on the input element)
- {@link #cfg!regex #regex} to specify a custom regular expression for validation

In addition, custom validations may be added:

- {@link #cfg!vtype #vtype} specifies a virtual type implementation from {@link Ext.form.field.VTypes} which can contain
  custom validation logic
- {@link #cfg!validator #validator} allows a custom arbitrary function to be called during validation

The details around how and when each of these validation options get used are described in the
documentation for {@link #method!getErrors #getErrors}.

By default, the field value is checked for validity immediately while the user is typing in the
field. This can be controlled with the {@link #cfg!validateOnChange #validateOnChange}, {@link #cfg!checkChangeEvents #checkChangeEvents}, and
{@link #cfg!checkChangeBuffer #checkChangeBuffer} configurations. Also see the details on Form Validation in the
{@link Ext.form.Panel} class documentation.

# Masking and Character Stripping

Text fields can be configured with custom regular expressions to be applied to entered values before
validation: see {@link #cfg!maskRe #maskRe} and {@link #cfg!stripCharsRe #stripCharsRe} for details.

# Example usage

    @example
    Ext.create('Ext.form.Panel', {
        title: 'Contact Info',
        width: 300,
        bodyPadding: 10,
        renderTo: Ext.getBody(),
        items: [{
            xtype: 'textfield',
            name: 'name',
            fieldLabel: 'Name',
            allowBlank: false  // requires a non-empty value
        }, {
            xtype: 'textfield',
            name: 'email',
            fieldLabel: 'Email Address',
            vtype: 'email'  // requires value to be a valid email address format
        }]
    });

items.name: allowBlank
items.text: Specify false to validate that the value's length is > 0

items.name: allowOnlyWhitespace
items.text:
Specify false to automatically trim the value before validating
the whether the value is blank. Setting this to false automatically
sets {@link #cfg!allowBlank #allowBlank} to false.

items.name: blankText
items.text: The error text to display if the **{@link #cfg!allowBlank #allowBlank}** validation fails

items.name: disableKeyFilter
items.text: Specify true to disable input keystroke filtering

items.name: emptyCls
items.text:
The CSS class to apply to an empty field to style the **{@link #cfg!emptyText #emptyText}**.
This class is automatically added and removed as needed depending on the current field value.

items.name: emptyText
items.text:
The default text to place into an empty field.

Note that normally this value will be submitted to the server if this field is enabled; to prevent this you can
set the {@link Ext.form.action.Action#cfg!submitEmptyText submitEmptyText} option of {@link Ext.form.Basic#method!submit Ext.form.Basic#submit} to
false.

Also note that if you use {@link #cfg!inputType inputType}:'file', {@link #cfg!emptyText #emptyText} is not supported and should be
avoided.

Note that for browsers that support it, setting this property will use the HTML 5 placeholder attribute, and for
older browsers that don't support the HTML 5 placeholder attribute the value will be placed directly into the input
element itself as the raw value. This means that older browsers will obfuscate the {@link #cfg!emptyText #emptyText} value for
password input fields.

items.name: enableKeyEvents
items.text: true to enable the proxying of key events for the HTML input field

items.name: enforceMaxLength
items.text: True to set the maxLength property on the underlying input field. Defaults to false

items.name: grow
items.text: true if this field should automatically grow and shrink to its content

items.name: growAppend
items.text:
A string that will be appended to the field's current value for the purposes of calculating the target field
size. Only used when the {@link #cfg!grow #grow} config is true. Defaults to a single capital "W" (the widest character in
common fonts) to leave enough space for the next typed character and avoid the field value shifting before the
width is adjusted.

items.name: growMax
items.text: The maximum width to allow when `{@link #cfg!grow #grow} = true`

items.name: growMin
items.text: The minimum width to allow when `{@link #cfg!grow #grow} = true`

items.name: maskRe
items.text:
An input mask regular expression that will be used to filter keystrokes (character being
typed) that do not match.
Note: It does not filter characters already in the input.

items.name: maxLength
items.text:
Maximum input field length allowed by validation. This behavior is intended to
provide instant feedback to the user by improving usability to allow pasting and editing or overtyping and back
tracking. To restrict the maximum number of characters that can be entered into the field use the
**{@link Ext.form.field.Text#cfg!enforceMaxLength enforceMaxLength}** option.

Defaults to Number.MAX_VALUE.

items.name: maxLengthText
items.text: Error text to display if the **{@link #cfg!maxLength maximum length}** validation fails
items.value: 'The maximum length for this field is {0}'

items.name: minLength
items.text: Minimum input field length required

items.name: minLengthText
items.text: Error text to display if the **{@link #cfg!minLength minimum length}** validation fails.
items.value: 'The minimum length for this field is {0}'

items.name: regex
items.text:
A JavaScript RegExp object to be tested against the field value during validation.
If the test fails, the field will be marked invalid using
either **{@link #cfg!regexText #regexText}** or **{@link #cfg!invalidText #invalidText}**.

items.name: regexText
items.text: The error text to display if **{@link #cfg!regex #regex}** is used and the test fails during validation

items.name: requiredCls
items.text: The CSS class to apply to a required field, i.e. a field where **{@link #cfg!allowBlank #allowBlank}** is false.

items.name: selectOnFocus
items.text: true to automatically select any existing field text when the field receives input focus

items.name: size
items.text:
An initial value for the 'size' attribute on the text input element. This is only used if the field has no
configured {@link #cfg!width #width} and is not given a width by its container's layout. Defaults to 20.

items.name: stripCharsRe
items.text:
A JavaScript RegExp object used to strip unwanted content from the value
during input. If `{@link #cfg!stripCharsRe stripCharsRe}` is specified,
every *character sequence* matching `{@link #cfg!stripCharsRe stripCharsRe}` will be removed.

items.name: validator
items.text:
A custom validation function to be called during field validation ({@link #method!getErrors #getErrors}).
If specified, this function will be called first, allowing the developer to override the default validation
process.

This function will be passed the following parameters:

items.name: value
items.text: The current field value

items.name: return
items.text:
- True if the value is valid
- An error message if the value is invalid

items.name: vtype
items.text: A validation type name as defined in {@link Ext.form.field.VTypes}

items.name: vtypeText
items.text:
A custom error message to display in place of the default message provided for the **`{@link #cfg!vtype #vtype}`** currently
set for this field. **Note**: only applies if **`{@link #cfg!vtype #vtype}`** is set, else ignored.

items.name: autosize
items.text:
Fires when the **{@link #method!autoSize #autoSize}** function is triggered and the field is resized according to the
{@link #cfg!grow #grow}/{@link #cfg!growMin #growMin}/{@link #cfg!growMax #growMax} configs as a result. This event provides a hook for the
developer to apply additional logic at runtime to resize the field if needed.

items.name: this
items.text: This text field

items.name: width
items.text: The new field width

items.name: keydown
items.text: Keydown input field event. This event only fires if **{@link #cfg!enableKeyEvents #enableKeyEvents}** is set to true.

items.name: this
items.text: This text field

items.name: keypress
items.text: Keypress input field event. This event only fires if **{@link #cfg!enableKeyEvents #enableKeyEvents}** is set to true.

items.name: this
items.text: This text field

items.name: keyup
items.text: Keyup input field event. This event only fires if **{@link #cfg!enableKeyEvents #enableKeyEvents}** is set to true.

items.name: this
items.text: This text field

items.name: autoSize
items.text:
Automatically grows the field to accomodate the width of the text up to the maximum field width allowed. This
only takes effect if {@link #cfg!grow #grow} = true, and fires the {@link #event!autosize #autosize} event if the width changes.

items.name: getErrors
items.text:
Validates a value according to the field's validation rules and returns an array of errors
for any failing validations. Validation rules are processed in the following order:

1. **Field specific validator**

    A validator offers a way to customize and reuse a validation specification.
    If a field is configured with a `{@link #cfg!validator #validator}`
    function, it will be passed the current field value.  The `{@link #cfg!validator #validator}`
    function is expected to return either:

    - Boolean `true`  if the value is valid (validation continues).
    - a String to represent the invalid message if invalid (validation halts).

2. **Basic Validation**

    If the `{@link #cfg!validator #validator}` has not halted validation,
    basic validation proceeds as follows:

    - `{@link #cfg!allowBlank #allowBlank}` : (Invalid message = `{@link #cfg!blankText #blankText}`)

        Depending on the configuration of `{@link #cfg!allowBlank #allowBlank}`, a
        blank field will cause validation to halt at this step and return
        Boolean true or false accordingly.

    - `{@link #cfg!minLength #minLength}` : (Invalid message = `{@link #cfg!minLengthText #minLengthText}`)

        If the passed value does not satisfy the `{@link #cfg!minLength #minLength}`
        specified, validation halts.

    -  `{@link #cfg!maxLength #maxLength}` : (Invalid message = `{@link #cfg!maxLengthText #maxLengthText}`)

        If the passed value does not satisfy the `{@link #cfg!maxLength #maxLength}`
        specified, validation halts.

3. **Preconfigured Validation Types (VTypes)**

    If none of the prior validation steps halts validation, a field
    configured with a `{@link #cfg!vtype #vtype}` will utilize the
    corresponding {@link Ext.form.field.VTypes} validation function.
    If invalid, either the field's `{@link #cfg!vtypeText #vtypeText}` or
    the VTypes vtype Text property will be used for the invalid message.
    Keystrokes on the field will be filtered according to the VTypes
    vtype Mask property.

4. **Field specific regex test**

    If none of the prior validation steps halts validation, a field's
    configured `{@link #cfg!regex #regex}` test will be processed.
    The invalid message for this test is configured with `{@link #cfg!regexText #regexText}`

items.name: value
items.text: The value to validate. The processed raw value will be used if nothing is passed.
Array of any validation errors

items.name: getRawValue
items.text:
Returns the raw String value of the field, without performing any normalization, conversion, or validation. Gets
the current value of the input element if the field has been rendered, ignoring the value if it is the
{@link #cfg!emptyText #emptyText}. To get a normalized and converted value see {@link #method!getValue #getValue}.
The raw String value of the field

items.name: isEqual
items.text: Override. Treat undefined and null values as equal to an empty string value.

items.name: onChange
items.text: If grow=true, invoke the autoSize method when the field's value is changed.

items.name: processRawValue
value
items.text: The unprocessed string value
The processed string value

items.name: reset
items.text:
Resets the current field value to the originally-loaded value and clears any validation messages.
Also adds **{@link #cfg!emptyText #emptyText}** and **{@link #cfg!emptyCls #emptyCls}** if the original value was blank.

items.name: selectText
items.text: Selects text in this field

items.name: start
items.text: The index where the selection should start

items.name: end
items.text: The index where the selection should end (defaults to the text length)

items.name: setValue
items.text:
Sets a data value into the field and runs the change detection and validation. Also applies any configured
{@link #cfg!emptyText #emptyText} for text fields. To set the value directly without these inspections see {@link #method!setRawValue #setRawValue}.

items.name: Ext.form.field.TextArea
items.text:
This class creates a multiline text field, which can be used as a direct replacement for traditional
textarea fields. In addition, it supports automatically {@link #cfg!grow growing} the height of the textarea to
fit its content.

All of the configuration options from {@link Ext.form.field.Text} can be used on TextArea.

Example usage:

    @example
    Ext.create('Ext.form.FormPanel', {
        title      : 'Sample TextArea',
        width      : 400,
        bodyPadding: 10,
        renderTo   : Ext.getBody(),
        items: [{
            xtype     : 'textareafield',
            grow      : true,
            name      : 'message',
            fieldLabel: 'Message',
            anchor    : '100%'
        }]
    });

Some other useful configuration options when using {@link #cfg!grow #grow} are {@link #cfg!growMin #growMin} and {@link #cfg!growMax #growMax}.
These allow you to set the minimum and maximum grow heights for the textarea.

**NOTE:** In some browsers, carriage returns ('\r', not to be confused with new lines)
will be automatically stripped out the value is set to the textarea. Since we cannot
use any reasonable method to attempt to re-insert these, they will automatically be
stripped out to ensure the behaviour is consistent across browser.

items.name: cols
items.text:
An initial value for the 'cols' attribute on the textarea element. This is only used if the component has no
configured {@link #cfg!width #width} and is not given a width by its container's layout.

items.name: enterIsSpecial
items.text:
True if you want the ENTER key to be classed as a special key and the {@link #event!specialkey #specialkey} event to be fired
when ENTER is pressed.

items.name: growAppend
items.text:
A string that will be appended to the field's current value for the purposes of calculating the target field
size. Only used when the {@link #cfg!grow #grow} config is true. Defaults to a newline for TextArea to ensure there is
always a space below the current line.

items.name: growMax
items.text: The maximum height to allow when {@link #cfg!grow #grow}=true

items.name: growMin
items.text: The minimum height to allow when {@link #cfg!grow #grow}=true

items.name: preventScrollbars
items.text:
true to prevent scrollbars from appearing regardless of how much text is in the field. This option is only
relevant when {@link #cfg!grow #grow} is true. Equivalent to setting overflow: hidden.

items.name: rows
items.text:
An initial value for the 'rows' attribute on the textarea element. This is only used if the component has no
configured {@link #cfg!height #height} and is not given a height by its container's layout. Defaults to 4.

items.name: autosize
items.text:
Fires when the {@link #method!autoSize #autoSize} function is triggered and the field is resized according to
the grow/growMin/growMax configs as a result. This event provides a hook for the developer
to apply additional logic at runtime to resize the field if needed.

items.name: autoSize
items.text:
Automatically grows the field to accomodate the height of the text up to the maximum field height allowed. This
only takes effect if {@link #cfg!grow #grow} = true, and fires the {@link #event!autosize #autosize} event if the height changes.

items.name: Ext.form.field.Time
items.text:
Provides a time input field with a time dropdown and automatic time validation.

This field recognizes and uses JavaScript Date objects as its main {@link #cfg!value #value} type (only the time portion of the
date is used; the month/day/year are ignored). In addition, it recognizes string values which are parsed according to
the {@link #cfg!format #format} and/or {@link #cfg!altFormats #altFormats} configs. These may be reconfigured to use time formats appropriate for
the user's locale.

The field may be limited to a certain range of times by using the {@link #cfg!minValue #minValue} and {@link #cfg!maxValue #maxValue} configs,
and the interval between time options in the dropdown can be changed with the {@link #cfg!increment #increment} config.

Example usage:

    @example
    Ext.create('Ext.form.Panel', {
        title: 'Time Card',
        width: 300,
        bodyPadding: 10,
        renderTo: Ext.getBody(),
        items: [{
            xtype: 'timefield',
            name: 'in',
            fieldLabel: 'Time In',
            minValue: '6:00 AM',
            maxValue: '8:00 PM',
            increment: 30,
            anchor: '100%'
        }, {
            xtype: 'timefield',
            name: 'out',
            fieldLabel: 'Time Out',
            minValue: '6:00 AM',
            maxValue: '8:00 PM',
            increment: 30,
            anchor: '100%'
       }]
    });

items.name: altFormats
items.text:
Multiple date formats separated by "|" to try when parsing a user input value and it doesn't match the defined
format.
items.value: "g:ia|g:iA|g:i a|g:i A|h:i|g:i|H:i|ga|ha|gA|h a|g a|g A|gi|hi|gia|hia|g|H|gi a|hi a|giA|hiA|gi A|hi A"

items.name: format
items.text:
The default time format string which can be overriden for localization support. The format must be valid
according to {@link Ext.Date#method!parse Ext.Date#parse}.

Defaults to `'g:i A'`, e.g., `'3:15 PM'`. For 24-hour time format try `'H:i'` instead.

items.name: increment
items.text: The number of minutes between each time value in the list.

items.name: invalidText
items.text: The error text to display when the time in the field is invalid.

items.name: maxText
items.text: The error text to display when the entered time is after {@link #cfg!maxValue #maxValue}.
items.value: "The time in this field must be equal to or before {0}"

items.name: maxValue
items.text:
The maximum allowed time. Can be either a Javascript date object with a valid time value or a string time in a
valid format -- see {@link #cfg!format #format} and {@link #cfg!altFormats #altFormats}.

items.name: minText
items.text: The error text to display when the entered time is before {@link #cfg!minValue #minValue}.
items.value: "The time in this field must be equal to or after {0}"

items.name: minValue
items.text:
The minimum allowed time. Can be either a Javascript date object with a valid time value or a string time in a
valid format -- see {@link #cfg!format #format} and {@link #cfg!altFormats #altFormats}.

items.name: pickerMaxHeight
items.text: The maximum height of the {@link Ext.picker.Time} dropdown.

items.name: selectOnTab
items.text: Whether the Tab key should select the currently highlighted item.

items.name: snapToIncrement
items.text: Specify as `true` to enforce that only values on the {@link #cfg!increment #increment} boundary are accepted.

items.name: submitFormat
items.text:
The date format string which will be submitted to the server. The format must be valid according to
{@link Ext.Date#method!parse Ext.Date#parse}.

Defaults to {@link #cfg!format #format}.

items.name: triggerCls
items.text:
An additional CSS class used to style the trigger button. The trigger will always get the {@link #cfg!triggerBaseCls #triggerBaseCls}
by default and triggerCls will be **appended** if specified.

items.name: createPicker
items.text: Creates the {@link Ext.picker.Time}

items.name: getErrors
items.text:
Runs all of Time's validations and returns an array of any errors. Note that this first runs Text's validations,
so the returned array is an amalgamation of all field errors. The additional validation checks are testing that
the time format is valid, that the chosen time is within the {@link #cfg!minValue #minValue} and {@link #cfg!maxValue #maxValue} constraints
set.

items.name: value
items.text: The value to get errors for (defaults to the current field value)
All validation errors for this field

items.name: onListSelectionChange
items.text: Handles a time being selected from the Time picker.

items.name: parseDate
items.text: Parses an input value into a valid Date object.

items.name: setLimit
items.text:
Updates either the min or max value. Converts the user's value into a Date object whose
year/month/day is set to the {@link #property!initDate #initDate} so that only the time fields are significant.

items.name: setMaxValue
items.text: Replaces any existing {@link #cfg!maxValue #maxValue} with the new time and refreshes the picker's range.

items.name: value
items.text: The maximum time that can be selected

items.name: setMinValue
items.text: Replaces any existing {@link #cfg!minValue #minValue} with the new time and refreshes the picker's range.

items.name: value
items.text: The minimum time that can be selected

items.name: syncSelection
items.text: Synchronizes the selection in the picker to match the current value

items.name: initDate
items.text:
This is the date to use when generating time values in the absence of either minValue
or maxValue.  Using the current date causes DST issues on DST boundary dates, so this is an
arbitrary "safe" date that can be any date aside from DST boundary dates.

items.name: Ext.form.field.Trigger
editable
items.text:
false to prevent the user from typing text directly into the field; the field can only have its value set via an
action invoked by the trigger.

true to prevent the user from changing the field, and hides the trigger. Supercedes the editable and hideTrigger
options if the value is true.

items.name: selectOnFocus
items.text:
true to select any existing text in the field immediately on focus. Only applies when
{@link #cfg!editable editable} = true

items.name: triggerBaseCls
items.text:
The base CSS class that is always added to the trigger button. The {@link #cfg!triggerCls #triggerCls} will be appended in
addition to this class.

items.name: triggerCls
items.text:
An additional CSS class used to style the trigger button. The trigger will always get the {@link #cfg!triggerBaseCls #triggerBaseCls}
by default and triggerCls will be **appended** if specified.

items.name: triggerNoEditCls
items.text: The CSS class that is added to the text field when component is read-only or not editable.

items.name: triggerWrapCls
items.text: The CSS class that is added to the div wrapping the trigger button(s).

items.name: getTriggerStateFlags
items.text:
Returns a set of flags that describe the trigger state. These are just used to easily
determine if the DOM is out-of-sync with the component's properties.

items.name: getTriggerWidth
items.text: Get the total width of the trigger button area.
The total trigger width

items.name: onBlur
items.text:
The default blur handling must not occur for a TriggerField, implementing this template method as emptyFn disables that.
Instead the tab key is monitored, and the superclass's onBlur is called when tab is detected

items.name: onTriggerClick
items.text:
The function that should handle the trigger's click event. This method does nothing by default until overridden
by an implementing function. See Ext.form.field.ComboBox and Ext.form.field.Date for sample implementations.

items.name: setEditable
items.text:
Sets the editable state of this field. This method is the runtime equivalent of setting the 'editable' config
option at config time.

items.name: editable
items.text:
True to allow the user to directly edit the field text. If false is passed, the user
will only be able to modify the field using the trigger. Will also add a click event to the text field which
will call the trigger.

items.name: setReadOnly
items.text:
Sets the read-only state of this field. This method is the runtime equivalent of setting the 'readOnly' config
option at config time.

items.name: readOnly
items.text:
True to prevent the user changing the field and explicitly hide the trigger. Setting
this to true will supercede settings editable and hideTrigger. Setting this to false will defer back to editable
and hideTrigger.

items.name: inputCell
items.text: A reference to the `TD` element wrapping the input element. Only set after the field has been rendered.

items.name: triggerEl
items.text: A composite of all the trigger button elements. Only set after the field has been rendered.

items.name: triggerWidth
items.text:
Width of the trigger element. Unless set explicitly, it will be
automatically calculated through creating a temporary element
on page. (That will be done just once per app run.)

items.name: triggerWrap
items.text: A reference to the `TABLE` element which encapsulates the input field and all trigger button(s). Only set after the field has been rendered.

items.name: email
items.text:
The function used to validate email addresses. Note that complete validation per the email RFC
specifications is very complex and beyond the scope of this class, although this function can be
overridden if a more comprehensive validation scheme is desired. See the validation section
of the [Wikipedia article on email addresses][1] for additional information. This implementation is
intended to validate the following types of emails:

- `barney@example.de`
- `barney.rubble@example.com`
- `barney-rubble@example.coop`
- `barney+rubble@example.com`
- `barney'rubble@example.com`
- `b.arne.y_r.ubbl.e@example.com`
- `barney4rubble@example.com`
- `barney4rubble!@example.com`
- `_barney+rubble@example.com`
- `"barney+rubble"@example.com`

[1]: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-mail_address

items.text: The email address
true if the RegExp test passed, and false if not.

items.name: url
items.text: The function used to validate URLs

items.name: value

true if the RegExp test passed, and false if not.

items.name: alphaMask
items.text: The keystroke filter mask to be applied on alpha input. Defaults to: /[a-z_]/i

items.name: alphanumMask
items.text: The keystroke filter mask to be applied on alphanumeric input. Defaults to: /[a-z0-9_]/i

items.name: Ext.form.FieldAncestor
items.text:
A mixin for {@link Ext.container.Container} components that are likely to have form fields in their
items subtree. Adds the following capabilities:

- Methods for handling the addition and removal of {@link Ext.form.Labelable} and {@link Ext.form.field.Field}
  instances at any depth within the container.
- Events ({@link #event!fieldvaliditychange #fieldvaliditychange} and {@link #event!fielderrorchange #fielderrorchange}) for handling changes to the state
  of individual fields at the container level.
- Automatic application of {@link #cfg!fieldDefaults #fieldDefaults} config properties to each field added within the
  container, to facilitate uniform configuration of all fields.

This mixin is primarily for internal use by {@link Ext.form.Panel} and {@link Ext.form.FieldContainer},
and should not normally need to be used directly. @docauthor Jason Johnston <jason@sencha.com>
